Based on my chemical knowledge, when halogenated organics (compounds containing halogens like chlorine, bromine, etc.) are mixed with non-oxidizing acids, the primary hazard is the generation of toxic gases. Halogenated organic compounds can decompose when exposed to acids, releasing toxic halogen gases such as hydrogen chloride (HCl), hydrogen bromide (HBr), or other halogenated gases.

This is a well-known chemical incompatibility in laboratory safety protocols. The reaction can lead to the formation of hydrogen halides which are toxic when inhaled and can cause severe respiratory issues.
